science.qualification: Photosphere color from a blackbody at the star's published temperature, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 6,112 K and log g 4.53 (u1 0.398, u2 0.295): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Campaign 1
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 13.4 days, fitted with starry to the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 1 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 0.67%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.14%, the light's own noise being 0.07%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. The period is the mean of three methods' periods (periodogram 6.59 d, wavelet 6.75 d, autocorrelation 6.75 d; periodogram peak 0.32), accepted by the criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43). The light repeats every 6.7 days, half the rotation period the catalogues print for the star: two groups of spots on opposite sides do that. The map is made at a tilt of 60°, worked out from the star's rotation speed, period and radius. Gaia DR3 lists 1 other star within 16 arcseconds, with 31% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · brightness map made here · Campaign 1

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#fff5f4, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in K2 campaign 1 (June to August 2014): the map's scale, 98% to 102% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 3.1% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · the star in its color over its brightness map · June to August 2014
